body:
@tkrugg 

> I see there is a certain level of compatibility with react and vue. It'd be be nice to check we can reach the same level of feature coverage in every flavour we have.

It should be pretty similar but I can try to reproduce these tests in react/vue/angular to compare the different solutions.

> There is nothing for angular but maybe we can work something out with puppeteer or cypress.

There is also an [Angular Testing Library](https://testing-library.com/docs/angular-testing-library/intro)

@francoischalifour 

> Did you spot some cases where this strategy hits limitation compared to the way we currently test our exposed API?

Not yet, but I only tested a very simple widget for now. Do you have something in mind?

@Haroenv 

> I think this is useful, but it needs a document where we write which kind of tests should be tested in which way to have a consistent experience

Yes, I think it could be documented the same way @francoischalifour  did for our [current testing guidelines](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1EUi72bcz9RzrlNrRrkIsLNDjsygpD0yN9ptjp8v57Hc/edit?pli=1).
